reviews.text: [h1]阿伟，你又在玩神碑了？[/h1] 作为一个线上线下打了差不多一千小时的游戏王玩家，当然不能错过《未元物质》这款打着“致敬游戏王”的肉鸽卡牌。目前浅浅的体验了下游戏（demo浅玩了一段时间），除了20费出场即胜利的类“艾克佐迪亚”之外，几乎没法在游戏里看到什么游戏王元素，但随着对局数渐渐增多，才从密密麻麻的棋子中挖出两个大字——碑批。 “神碑”卡组放在游戏王中也是一个相当特殊的卡组，卡组并不以削减对手生命值来取得胜利，取而代之的是尽可能的阻断敌人展开并破坏敌人卡组，让对手抽不了卡，折磨自己的同时也在折磨敌人，核心是能够在对方回合发动速攻魔法卡的场地魔法神碑之泉，《未元物质》的游戏思路与神碑卡组几乎如出一辙，对方没有生命值设定，只有对手没卡可抽，或者对手的卡片（只有怪兽）累计被破坏十张，才能判定为玩家的胜利，有时甚至压根就不需要战斗阶段，卡组可以形成一定的构筑，但卡组构筑的目的是卡组破坏，敌我双方都是如此，这也意味着，原本玩家准备的那组展开多米诺骨牌，很容易就被对方从中间环节阻断，但游戏没有神碑内战那般坐牢，游戏中的小系统格外的多，效果的发动也遵循后发先至的规则（可惜没有自排连锁），几乎所有的效果都是必发效果，预测下后期的进阶操作应该可以用一系列效果去骗康，游戏中卡牌的DBG构筑深度和可玩度都相当高。 美中不足的时，游戏似乎并不打算开放多人模式，折磨电脑的乐趣怎么也比不上折磨对手来的舒服，不过单人模式下目测似乎还是有大约几十小时的主线流程可以玩，游戏的类型还是roguelite，随着卡池解锁进度增加游戏到后期应该会变得更耐玩和好玩吧。

你知道这游戏赢的卡牌游戏的方式有哪些吗？ 除了干掉的对手的卡牌，居然还能把对手的卡牌偷了，让他没有牌，哈哈哈哈第一次这样操作的时候笑死我了对手打出的卡牌居然还能偷了让他输掉对局。 对手的卡牌融合到很强了，看起来好厉害的样子，但是他马上就是我的啦，可以偷取或者交换过来，你看起来变强了其实都是为我做的嫁衣，狂喜。但是自己融合了很强的卡牌被拿来攻击自己的时候真是想吐血，只想大声说：你怎么可以这样玩，不讲武德！！ 挺有趣且独特的卡牌机制，对了装备牌只能有一张，别第二次选择装备的时候把自己强力装备给搞丢咯哦

《未元物质》是一款肉鸽构筑卡牌游戏，相比与一众尖塔、战棋、炉石的类似者，本作倒是更像游戏王，怪兽的召唤机制类似于link连接的加法规则，也借助每次融合召唤己方都能抽1牌、带来了牌组规划与回合内源源不断的操作空间、在费用=攻击力的卡牌战力机制上、依靠特效的多样与卡牌的相互搭配、提供了较为丰富的策略性。 整体价格便宜、UI简洁、系统机制独特、玩法较为有趣，但就目前几个小时的游戏体验，感觉不是很耐玩。主要是由于关卡流程较为固定、只能依靠构筑的随机性；而不同boss的套牌则有几率相同、使得挑战体验相似；不同关卡更多在于推进剧情（？）、有些降低可重玩性。

零号病患那些boss是咋想的，说书说十分钟然后封我全格全怪集体打我脸，我一点办法没有，打牌王好的没学到怎么净学封锁了？鉴定为玩香格里拉茧玩的 还有那个被打叠手里高费牌的，跟复制自己到手牌的史莱姆无限循环，永远打不死，制作组是不是觉得自己很幽默，看我设计出来个无敌组合赶紧凑一起恶心一波玩家！ 这两个恶心人的boss卡组并非百分百打不过，但是往往需要很极端的构筑，而且道中会很不好过。这个游戏其他方面完成度相对比较高，所以特地给boss搞恶心人卡组绝对是故意的。
小品级游戏吧，平衡一般，快攻卡组咔咔咔就连杀boss到无尽了。。不知道后面有没有其他路子
最后几张卡怎么解锁的？一点提示也没有 无尽后期boss来来回回就那么几套，完全脚打，毫无挑战性 选卡时咱们能加个跳过吗？我真不需要那么多卡，每次都要商店卖卡很烦耶 披着肉鸽皮的线性游戏，主线过完就没什么可以玩了。 ---- 邪恶傀儡师和生化危害联动有bug，会弹窗报错
爽哥严选！ 但是选卡不能跳过就尼玛逆天 10卡卡组打到32卡被对面ntr走我大哥生了一地4阶怪把我薄纱 还有就是套路有点少
好玩，但是游玩过程中遇到一些问题：1. bug，遇到一次声音卡住，和电钻一样 2. 棋子卡组纯废物 3. 带鱼屏全屏显示bug
可持续游玩度很差，一个是没有局外成长的内容，一个是除了卡牌解锁之外就没有其他什么东西了 作为肉鸽游戏几乎都有的遗物系统，这游戏里对应的是装备，但装备只能带一个就…… 杀戮尖塔我虽然也没什么动力玩很多把，但好歹还有四个英雄分别解锁一下，希望能在后续继续优化吧

Simple to figure out yet complex and challenging! Really addicting game play loop that focuses on unique card combos. I used to find card games too complex to play, but I recently got into card games with stuff like Inscryption and Magic. This game uses a simple style where your attack and health are the same number, so it's quick to figure out! The bosses do put up quite a fight but they make you feel like a genius when you manage to beat them. This almost feels like a puzzle game at times with figuring out combos on top of combos to really lay into the enemy, Has a story mode plus an endless mode to see how far you get. It's rouge lite where dying will require you to start over, but you're constantly unlocking new cards and decks to experiment with on future runs! Highly recommend! (Plus the music is bumpin')

Being completely honest, this game blew my mind. Wasn't expecting much, but it's actually pretty fun and thrilling. At first it seems like an easy game, but it suddenly gets hard and it's pretty easy for you to lose and have to restart your run lol. A really nice card and roguelike game. Mechanics are simple, yet hard to master. Surprisingly awesome game!

Incredibly deep strategies in this game! The yugioh feel is there (not mana based, your deck and hand are your resources), with a lot to make it unique as well (you can lose if your deck is shorter than your life, cards have a single power value equal to the number of tributes required). The many different decks play extremely different, and really require you to play in a completely different way to win. The biggest success of this game is how the card effects use the game's many unique mechanics to create many unique deck types. Incredible game!

Updated 01/19 - I have changed this to a positive review based on the most recent playtest (which I would highly recommend opting into). What I said below is still valid about the depth of the encounters being held back by a lot of the surrounding gameplay mechanics, but the playtest is an amazing step in the right direction. As it stands, an experienced player is more likely to abandon an endless run than to lose it, but now you can make your decks more focused and enjoy different playstyles a lot easier. This is a good game for someone breaking into the genre and a fun afternoon or two for someone that has played a lot of deck builders. This is one of those that make me wish Steam had a neutral recommendation. The card design is very cool, but the actual content is held back by the power of low cost cards and the very punishing damage system. The damage system forces the game to avoid complex situations and instead resort to a series of cheap chip damage encounters. If it didn't keep things simple and easy, it'd be impossible to avoid a loss as you can only afford to take 1 or 2 damage an encounter unless you run specific decks. This also means that each fight (including boss fights) will last about 2 turns and never involve much thinking beyond what mob attacks what creature to minimize wasting your attacks. You never really ramp up to anything as the best ways of playing big cards involve effects from cheap cards and other cheap cards will often nullify the big cards anyways. Despite the issues I have with the design, I don't want to dissuade anyone from buying it if they are newer to deck-builders. I think it's a good card game for someone breaking into the genre as it is very straightforward but has some complex combos to explore as well. For experienced players - expect some cool cards and neat ideas to mess around with, but don't expect the game to push you much or allow for deep exploration of those ideas. I beat all 9 of the story missions across about 5 hours of gameplay without a loss, but it felt less like I built a good deck (I didn't) and more like the battles had to be very winnable to minimize unavoidable damage.

Great mechanics marred by the lack of a decent AI to pilot them, meaning that most of your game is spent doing puzzle-adjacent tasks rather than using your deck against another deck. The few times that this does happen - the boss at the end of a run or 4-floor phase of an Endless run - you'll see the AI do its best imitation of early generation Yugioh AI by making nearly every legal move possible, to its own detriment. There are some genuinely great ideas here that I hope carry on to another game, but if you've got any reasonable amount of experience with card games like this, you'll not only be able to break balance easily but also have no need to do so. Had this been a multiplayer or a straight "duel vs semi-competent AI decks" focused game instead of masking behind a tacked-on "Roguelike" framework, I'd likely be leaving a positive review instead. If you do buy in, know that their "must allow us analytics with no opt-out" EULA is a thing (as are firewalls, among other anti-invasive options), and that feedback is limited mainly to their Discord. Also, for a game with "100+" cards, locking a large portion of them behind a slow ~39 level grind where a winning run gains around 2-3 levels means you'll be making a lot of similar decks.

游戏挺好，提点意见。一个是直到通关存的一百多金币都没用上，不知道是我太倒霉还是金币挑战的出现频率远远大于商店。然后是在删牌只能去商店删的前提下（而且没有任何代价），平时奖励的卡牌无法选择什么都不拿是否有点不合适。底子是好底子，但是数值、平衡、难度曲线什么的还需要优化下。 无尽模式后再编辑：一些牌（比如4级控制卡组大哥）的能力如果也可以选择不发动就好了（眼睁睁看着法力池被金币克拉肯粘液怪召唤浪费）。然后就是无尽成型后的确感受不到难度（30张打我70张谁才是boss），顺便克拉肯的再生那个boss应该是最麻烦的了，虽然不是赢不了但这么精简的卡组太容易实现无限了（建议粘液怪发动次数改为每回合x次什么的……） 其他平衡方面的建议：对玩家牌组上限进行限制，比如30张以后开始获得debuff之类的，可以选择不拿奖励牌，增加删牌的代价和手段（老套但管用…）；目前的心脏ai好喜欢各种让3级冒名者返场站前排，这个ai不太聪明的样子（当然也可能是因为这boss实力上游制作人的怜悯…但考虑到粘液怪克拉肯的强度我觉得大概没有这个考虑），也许可以优化一下。 目前还在玩，后续有意见还会更新

This would be a neutral review if it was an option. At first I really liked the concepts of this game. Card fusions made for faced paced flashy gameplay, that allowed you to really push cards out on to the field quickly. Your cards get damaged and removed from your deck when killed, so you have to make careful decisions. Every card has interesting abilities that allow for a lot of interesting combo potential. But all of these things I described quickly started to crack under pressure when I advanced in game difficulty. The card fusion mechanic is fun, but it really promotes trying to win in 1-3 turns. The enemy is able to generate so many cards, especially boss fights, that you have to win as quickly and aggressively as possible. Unlike other card games like Monster Train or Slay the Spire, your battles will feel very quick. It doesn't help that when your cards are destroyed, they are removed from your deck until you can find a healing node to put them back in. That means trying to minimize enemy attacks on your cards by either destroying the enemy quickly, or utilizing defensive strategies. It forces you to avoid risky plays and reduces your play options. All of the cards have really crazy fun abilities but more often than not, really cheap 1 cost cards can completely nullify expensive 4 cost cards. You could play a really good combo of cards and get a couple 3 or 4 costs on the field, but then the enemies 1 costs will just run over them. Also, the enemy doesn't have to worry about its health like you do. All of those abilities that are really risky and can cause a lot of self damage? The AI will happily use those and cause extra damage to itself so that it can hurt you, and its almost impossible to prevent. I found the bosses on harder difficulties to be really frustrating. On turn one I essentially have to wait 2-3 minutes to watch them create a crazy head start of a board state. Also, even if you have some crazy start with your deck on turn 1 on a boss fight, you still have to deal with the aftermath of a fight. Every time you kill one of their cards, they will draw a card to their hand. That mean's on the following turn after attacking their units, you're almost guaranteed damage. You get to draw cards when you lose units too, but you want to prevent this because of how damage works. Losing a unit means you lose the card from your deck. Damage doesn't reset after a battle either, so losing units is really bad. So the ability to draw cards because your units die feels like a last ditch effort to survive, rather than a fun way to get access to more cards in your deck. But the fun kicker to this is that the AI benefits from this mechanic the most since it doesn't care about its health. You just wiped its whole board? better get ready cause its hand is now full of cards to play. I don't know.... The quality is there to some degree. You can tell some passion and effort was put into the game. I like the art style, the abilities of cards is varied and fun, and the fusion mechanic is really unique. The game runs really well. I like a lot of the synergies I did discover. But ultimately there was too much getting in the way of the fun I was having. I think I can definitely overcome the challenges in the game too, I just found myself not enjoying the attempt. I think it just comes down to the fact that I don't enjoy some of the design choices. My overall score is a 2/5. With how many games exist in the world at this point, there are simply just better card games to play at the same price point.
拿着路上一张一张捡起来的垃圾卡组和boss多出来十张甚至九张牌的成型体系卡组打，真当人人都是蟹哥？

[h1] 《Primateria》：有新意，但也仅仅是有新意[/h1] [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote] 《未元物质》（《Primateria》）是一款由Yfrit Games开发、Surefire.Games发行的肉鸽卡牌游戏。个人的卡牌经验不算丰富，只是玩过尖塔以及一种类炉石作品，而这部《未元物质》就恰好是一种我没见过的船新类型——据说是致敬《游戏王》，不过我刚巧没有玩过游戏王，只是保留着小时候对这个古老的卡牌IP残留下来的零星记忆，因此对我来说本作的模式就显得很新颖，但是也仅仅是新颖而已，游戏在实际内容量上还是有些不足。 [h2]画面还算好看[/h2] 游戏的UI还算不错，尽管标题页面的观感非常简陋，但是游戏内的布局像模像样，比如牌堆、随从展示、卡面图案等等都有着不错的质感，游戏核心的「怪物融合」机制还有着华丽的特效，而一些战斗动画也是渲染的有声有色，束缚、燃烧、破碎等效果丰富了游戏的视觉表现，总体感觉打起来比较华丽，战斗也很流畅。 [h2]玩法有点独特[/h2] 相较于寻常的卡牌游戏，本作在玩法上无疑是另辟蹊径。尽管随从战场和卡组管理页面都是满满的炉石style，不过从游戏体验上跟炉石可以说是大相径庭：[b]一方面本作丢掉了卡牌游戏里的血量设计，玩家的获胜条件变为消耗光敌人的卡组，[/b]对于见多了卡池循环的肉鸽卡牌来说这算是个新奇的概念，从评论区的科普来看这个是致敬了游戏王里的「神碑」卡组；[b]另一方面本作也没有费用限制，一回合可以无限打出卡牌，不过加入了一个特殊的「怪物融合」，[/b]比如2费卡需要通过打出两张1费卡进行融合才能打出，3费卡则需要2费+1费的怪物，以此类推。这极大加速了游戏流程，因为你上手的卡牌可能一次性就全打出去了，尽管之后的过牌缓慢不过也没有太多牌可以打。 [h2]模式非常肉鸽[/h2] 至于游戏的模式则是以肉鸽爬塔为主，除了比较短的教程以外，游戏还有任务和无尽两个模式，其中任务模式相当于剧情模式，会有一些文本描述，但这不重要，咱玩卡牌从来就不是为了看剧情，况且剧情可以说是卡牌游戏里最不重要的一环。任务模式有三大关，每大关里有三小关，所以一共是九关剧情模式。当然你也可以一上来就在无尽模式里驰骋，不过剧情关卡也有一定教学作用，最好是熟悉牌组以后再去无尽关卡里闯荡。 [h2]总结[/h2] 总的来说，《未元物质》即使对卡牌老鸟来说都称得上颇具新意，不过尝鲜之后，本作的核心玩法到底能不能撑起一个圈子还有待商榷。毕竟本作跟寻常的卡牌游戏比起来有太多不同，而如果你一直追寻的就是这样一款玩法新颖的卡牌游戏，那么不妨来试试这部看起来很帅、打起来更帅的《未元物质》。

Innovative monster upgrades by fusing two or more together, some real goofy fun cards that remind me of hearthstone. An Endless mode that is rogue like, it keeps on getting harder until you die. If you're into card games there a lot here for you to enjoy. Only bad thing I can say is UI in the level select is not the best, but the arenas look amazing!
游戏设计上有缺陷，比如卡牌在束缚条件下的触发不应该是束缚后马上触发技能。

[h1]游玩感受[/h1] 打开本作一看，还以为又是小成本的低创卡牌游戏，不过细细的品味了几个小时之后，上手之后才发现本作意外的还行，虽然美术没太喜欢，但是玩法上还是看的出下了很多功夫的，价格不贵倒是值得一玩。 首先来说他并非影之诗那般每回合卡费用式的卡牌玩法，而是彻底取消费用的限制，用从低到高的连锁召唤方式尽可能的堆叠出更多的高级卡在场上，就如同金字塔一般，场上的三个一费卡能够召唤手牌的三费卡，游戏的目标也就变成了如何用手牌组建出更强的旗子消灭对方，消灭对方卡牌数为十就算成功，这墓地为十的苛刻条件，也就意味着进攻才是王道，快攻阵容也就成了我开荒最喜欢用的阵容，能将旗子的进攻能力发挥到极致并滚起雪球，大幅度减少对方发育的机会。 [h1]游玩的不足体验[/h1] 不过目前体验下来，游戏虽然是在玩棋子之间的配合，但其实目前的各个流派之中，各个棋子的联动效果并不是那么的明显，各个卡组的玩法区别并不是很大，游戏仍然需要许多更好的设计去丰富游戏，目前的内容更像是万丈高楼的地基，后续变成什么样子仍然需要制作组的优化更新。 后续也可以更新更多有趣的挑战关卡，游戏的剧情关卡只有九关目前也太过单薄了，以无尽模式为卖点来说游戏的重复游玩的吸引力还不够，可以试着出一些有意思的新模式来丰富一下游戏内容，毕竟我觉得游戏的底子还是蛮不错的。 [code]欢迎参观我的： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/7421824]双鱼星✪ω✪皇家飛机场[/url] 如果你喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到。[/code]

When it was just a demo, I was excited. Played the demo a few times. When it finally launched I bought as soon as I found out. For the first few hours, it was fun. Then you can just blow through the "story" with relative ease. The system encourages broken combo, which is fine but if you can frequently win the game in the first turn, whatever the opponent throws at you doesn't really matter. An infinite combo can be found relatively easy in the "starter set" that you get when you start the game. There are other interesting strategies but they don't seem to be as viable. Damage on your "character" is persistent in this game. Taking damage just for limited removal is horrible. To top it off, the power up de-emphasize the importance of deckbuilding a lot. This game is a lot closer to a dueling game (Yugioh) than a dungeon crawler (think slay the spire) so it's a bit of a bummer. You can get away with a lot of bad decisions thanks to some OP power up like: * Summon a level 5 when most cards are only at level 4. So far, I only know that one "hidden" card at level 5. * Add +1 to all cards on your side. The only thing left is endless mode which can become challenging if you keep going. However, I don't enjoy "endless" anything. It feels aimless and unsatisfying. Should I save my potion for the final show down? Should I unload everything I have since this is the final battle? I died stupidly last run but I was so close, should I do one more run? Nope, there is no end. At the current state and price, I can't recommend it. But do try out the demo, the game does have fresh ideas. Be aware that the full game, at the time of writing will be just a little more on that: * An endless mode * A lot of new cool cards but what you manage to build with the existing card pools is already too strong, you are just going through the motions most times.

[h1]怪物融合，玩法有趣的打牌游戏！[/h1] 《未元物质》是一款由Yfrit Games开发，Surefire.Games发行的轻度肉鸽卡牌游戏，不过，作为目前市面上竞争激烈的肉鸽卡牌类游戏，自然是需要一点自己特色。经过一些粗浅的游玩，就体验来说，这款游戏的卡牌，走的是炉石传说和游戏王这种怪物卡牌路子，还是有两把刷子的。那么今天，我们来打牌！ 《未元物质》作为一款轻度肉鸽卡牌游戏，首先在玩法上，如官方所说，与目前市场上主流的卡牌游戏不同，不同于依靠手牌来打出各种伤害，消减对方血量的玩法，放弃了血量这一元素，游戏的核心机制围绕在怪物数量和破坏次数而展开。 在游戏中，玩家只能够根据手牌中怪物的点数，来逐渐让怪物全部上场，高等级怪物需要低等级怪物作为素材进行融合，除非有特定卡牌效果的怪物，能够直接上场，其他卡牌，都需要经过这一流程。这意味着，不管你是运气多差，只要卡组构筑没有问题，那么最终，都能够在技术层面上，整出一个不错的怪物组合。 同时各种具有特殊效果的卡牌的存在，例如复制手牌、指定其他怪物承受行动束缚等，也让游玩的趣味性，更上一层。不单单是停留在比拼怪物数值大小上面。 简单举个例子，你手中有一张复制手牌和能够指定其他怪物承受束缚从而再次攻击的怪物卡。你能够将打出的手牌进行复制一张出来，表面上来看，复制一张高等级的卡牌，会是比较好的效果，但由于指定束缚这个东西，反而让你拥有数量更多的低等级怪物卡牌，会有更高的优势。数量够多，一回合打穿对面也是可行的。 这就是本作让人上头的地方了，游戏内融合、卡牌效果、死亡继承等众多机制相互配合，提供了足够的策略性给到玩家，同样的一个手牌，根据玩家打牌顺序的不同，能够走的路子也是各有差异。 整体来看，《未元物质》确实算是不错一款游戏，玩起来的新意很足，就内容体验上来说，是不错的，不过目前内容方面，还不算很充分，多少有点靠无尽模式撑场面的意思了。同时，UI设计和画面效果，虽然透露着一股子简陋风，但熟悉以后，反而觉得颇具特色。不清楚后续官方会不会继续优化画面效果和特效表现方面的内容，如果能够给高等级怪物出场整个小CG进去，想想都刺激。 至于卡牌方面，一贯的强度、成型速度及难度、平衡性等问题，则是与游戏的众多可玩流派和玩家重复游玩的动力息息相关，还需要官方大花力气的。 [code]双语评测，认准我们： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]双语评测[/url] Make Chinese and English speaker feel at home： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]Bilingual Curator[/url][/code]

Game's awesome. It's sort of like Yu-gi-oh, but here's a brief run-down of gameplay: You start by drawing your hand, which consists entirely of monster/creature/unit cards. Each card has a mana value associated with it 1-4. Unlike in other Roguelike Deckbuilders where there is a set pool of mana/energy that refreshes each turn and playing cards deducts from that mana, you don't have a system like that here. Instead, you can play creatures with mana value 1 immediately from your hand for free. To summon creatures of mana value 2 or more you must 'fuse' creatures whose mana value exactly equal that creature. Those creatures used for fusion are held within that newly summoned creature as mana. You can attack other creatures using 1 or more creatures you have whose mana value exceeds that targetted creature, and if successful, kills that creature but 'binds' your creature preventing it from attacking for the rest of the turn. Your opponent also plays by the same rules, and if they have creatures remaining they can use those to attack your creatures. Each time a creature of yours dies you take 1 damage, and if the total damage you recieved is 10 or more, you lose and damage carries over (but there are opportunities to heal). This game is very much about amassing awesome combos turn 1, FTK simulator effectively. You'll very likely have a lot of fun, as I have.

A Surprisingly Deep Deckbuilder with Strong Archetypes this game deserves more popularity. People say this game is similar to Yu-Gi-Oh!, but I’ve never played that, so I can’t speak to how much it borrows from it. What I can say is that the card mechanics here feel well thought-out and make deck building genuinely enjoyable. Cards are clearly designed with distinct archetypes in mind—things like token generation, multiple attacks per turn, cycling , or sacrificing health for greater value. Primateria, developed by Yfrit Games and published by Surefire.Games, is a roguelike deck-builder that embraces unpredictability, experimentation, and mechanical freedom as its defining traits. Rather than mimicking the structure of more rigid card battlers, it builds itself around a fusion-based system where cards can be combined, transformed, empowered, and even reimagined mid-combat. This design makes Primateria feel far more fluid than the typical turn-based deck-builder. The game encourages improvisation not only because you can play multiple cards without the usual mana restrictions, but because card evolution — and de-evolution — is part of its core loop. Each run becomes a sandbox of shifting strategies, a place where even weak cards can grow into powerhouse tools with the right fusion or where a strong card may revert and force you to pivot quickly. The world that frames these mechanics is equally imaginative. Primateria casts you as a “Polupus,” a strange being navigating a mythic, surreal universe populated by gods, esoteric creatures, and cosmic threats. The story mode gives this strange universe context, but it’s the visual direction and conceptual creativity that make the world feel alive. Enemies, abilities, relics, and even card art reflect the game’s surreal themes, giving the experience a sense of mystical tension. Rather than being a simple backdrop, the world serves as a thematic extension of the game’s chaotic philosophy: everything is mutable, everything changes form, and nothing remains fixed for long. This reinforces the idea that each run isn’t merely a sequence of battles but a journey through a volatile universe where adaptability is the ultimate skill. Primateria’s greatest strength lies in its variety and flexibility. With more than a hundred cards spanning multiple abilities, elemental synergies, and fusion paths, no two decks play the same. The roguelike structure ensures that even a strong knowledge of the card pool doesn’t guarantee predictable outcomes. Some runs feel blessed with perfect synergies; others demand ingenuity and resourcefulness. The ability to fuse cards mid-battle creates dynamic turns where a single decision can snowball into powerful combos or collapse into unintended consequences. These moments — the improvised victories, the narrow escapes, the accidental power spikes — are the heart of Primateria’s appeal. They make each run feel distinctive, rewarding players who enjoy discovery and experimentation. The game also benefits from a generous suite of modes. Beyond the main story, there are prebuilt decks for learning, endless modes for pushing limits, and later updates added features like a deck editor and boss rush. These additions significantly extend replay value, providing multiple ways to explore the fusion system and the card pool. For players who enjoy tuning builds, experimenting with archetypes, or pushing themselves against escalating difficulty, the game offers a solid amount of content and customization. The steady stream of updates and patches also reflects a clear commitment from the developers, helping balance out mechanics and adding features requested by the community. However, the same elements that make Primateria feel fresh can also make it uneven or overwhelming. The randomness at the core of its design — from card rewards to combat pacing — can sometimes make runs feel more dependent on luck than strategy. While many roguelikes embrace randomness, Primateria’s fusion-driven system can amplify that volatility, especially when a few unlucky fusions derail a promising deck. Players who prefer structured, controlled deck-building may find this philosophy frustrating. Similarly, the learning curve may feel steep, not because the rules are complicated individually, but because there are so many interacting systems: adaptive mana, dual graveyard mechanics, card evolution tiers, positioning, and varying combat synergies all contribute to its complexity. Thematically, the game’s surreal world and dark-fantasy aesthetic are distinctive but might not appeal to everyone. While they add personality and atmosphere, they can also make the experience feel abstract and detached. Additionally, the absence of a strong narrative throughline means that the emotional stakes rely more on mechanics and worldbuilding than on story. For some, this lack of narrative depth complements the roguelike structure; for others, it may make the journey feel less anchored. Despite these shortcomings, Primateria shines as a creative, imaginative, and bold entry in the roguelike deck-builder genre. It thrives on chaos — not carelessly, but intentionally — inviting players into a system that rewards flexibility, experimentation, and creative problem-solving. It is a game that encourages you to try wild combinations, embrace the unpredictable, and refine your understanding of its mechanics through repeated failure and experimentation. While not ideal for players seeking highly controlled, mathematically rigid deck-building experiences, it is an excellent choice for those who enjoy the thrill of discovery, the surprise of emergent strategies, and the satisfaction of turning an improvised idea into a triumphant win. In the end, Primateria stands out because it is unafraid to be different. It combines a surreal world, a fusion-driven card system, and a roguelike structure into an experience that feels alive, unstable, and creatively rewarding. For players who appreciate games that challenge traditional design boundaries, it offers a distinctive and deeply replayable journey. Rating: 8/10

Yugioh + Hearthstone + Slay The Spire with some adjustments that make the Yugioh actually work. Fusions regress to their original cards when you destroy them, meaning you still have material even if you lose your boss monster. You can attack a target with multiple creatures, meaning that walling is more about building up board interactions rather than just having a high stat card. Beating over creatures damages life points, 1 per, and players have 10 LP. There's three front row and two back row slots, and the back row can't be attacked until the front is gone. All of this makes the board state actually quite dynamic. You can rotate your enemy's cards to open up vulnerabilities, swarm over big creatures, take a lot of damage if you don't protect your swarm, tactically steal and debuff and discard creatures to open up weakpoints, etc. You are still reliant on your hand not bricking, but every fusion draws you a card and so it's *much* less bad than it could be. The art, design, and writing are also charming. They're weird and indie, but they work, and I'll take club penguin illustration homages over ai slopcards any day. I'll update the review as I play deeper, but if you like indie ccgs this is a pretty solid one at first glance. Edit: Oh yeah you can get extremely bricked still lmao. Statistically it shouldn't happen too often, but if it happens you do just lose the run. Drawing on damage helps mitigate, and it's not nearly as bad as yugioh or other yugiohlikes, but it can be a little frustrating in a roguelike format.
